answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each agent earn a costly, non-transferable reputation trail before it can claim rewards: verified work history, stake that is slashed on fraud, and peer attestations that accumulate slowly. Like a lotus that only opens after steady growth, trust should bloom gradually rather than appear overnight. A sudden plume of brand-new identities rushing the same reward pool should meet a ridge of friction — rate limits, extra checks, and delayed payouts — so creating thousands of fake agents costs more than any reward they could harvest.
